findings.evidence: “like the entrypoint, write it literally wherever $WORK appears” repeats the shell-session explanation at lines 49–50.
findings.fix: Keep the instructions to record and reuse both absolute paths, but consolidate the shell-session explanation into one sentence at entrypoint resolution. Record the duplicate wording as redundant.

findings.evidence: “On an offline or no-write request, do not run it” gives only a permission-relaxation path. The shipped offline scenario explicitly supplies an existing inventory and expects the flow to start at recommend.
findings.fix: Split the inventory step: with an owner-supplied snapshot for this project and workstream, disclose its freshness and resume at recommend without refreshing; without a usable snapshot, ask before relaxing the offline restriction. Keep no-write requests out of the plan-writing and apply steps.

findings.evidence: “set up a cross-AI execution runner” and “a faster alternative, not a replacement” distinguish setup from gsd-settings but not from launching or troubleshooting a live cross-AI run.
findings.fix: Use when asked to set up or migrate a GSD project's .planning/config.json, pick models per tier, wire installed skills to planner or executor agents, or configure cross-AI plan review and execution. Inventory the project, propose changes, and preview them before applying. Also use to render or upgrade cross-ai.mjs with ensure-runner or merge cross-ai.mjs.new. For live dispatches and retry handling, use ai-kit-cross-ai; for advanced GSD tuning or integrations, use gsd-settings or gsd-config.

findings.evidence: “Subcommand reference” repeats the core commands and the edited-runner readiness matrix already explained in the workflow. The body is 417 lines and about 32 KB despite the available task-gated references.
findings.fix: Keep the v2 commands beside their approval steps. Put the full readiness matrix in references/runner.md under the existing ensure-runner trigger, and use a one-line lookup pointer in the body. Replace the duplicated routine flag list with a pointer to the entrypoint's subcommand help.

findings.evidence: “run the dry run again and compare its rows with the approved ones” refers only to config-key rows. The CLI reports runner artifacts separately, so a create, replace, or .new outcome can change without any dotted-key row changing.
findings.fix: At the approval gate, show and compare both the config diff and the runner artifact disposition, including whether the active script changes and the permissions of the resulting hook. Obtain fresh approval when either differs; retain the caveat that a concurrent edit can still land after the preview.

findings.evidence: “Chooses router-backed models per tier without a scored catalog” conflicts with the detailed routers-only scenario, which expects unresolved tier choices and no invented model. The JSON case supplies no inventory. The migration fixture also has no v1 models or model_overrides leaves to exercise the managed-key removal gate.
findings.fix: Bind the JSON cases to deterministic inventories or to the existing fixture builder. Assert that unscored tier choices remain open until approved, and use a migration fixture with actual v1 override leaves so the test can compare the exact preview rows with the transcript before apply.

findings.evidence: “write a README for my personal dotfiles repository” is typical of the easy negatives. The 8/8 split mostly tests unrelated requests and does not challenge the boundaries with adjacent GSD configuration and runner-dispatch tasks.
findings.fix: Keep the balanced split but replace several easy negatives with realistic requests to launch an existing cross-ai.mjs, handle a live quota stop, configure GSD integration credentials, or tune advanced GSD settings. Add an implicit positive for a user who wants their installed skills and different models assigned to the project's planner and executor without naming the curated flow.

findings.evidence: “it makes resolve-model return an empty model for every agent without an override” is contradicted by the checked-out gsd-core resolver and tests/test_ai_kit_gsd_curated_config_matrix.py:145: gsd-core 1.22.0 can return a Claude tier alias.
findings.fix: Keep the curated unset rule, but distinguish it from the release-dependent resolver behavior. State that newer gsd-core can return native Claude aliases under omit and can ignore an omit inherited solely from shared defaults. Probe the target's resolve-model behavior before claiming a specific effect.

findings.evidence: “gets one wait and the same lane again” conflicts with the mandatory sibling procedure at skills/ai-kit-cross-ai/SKILL.md:341–352, which requires a confirmed one-shot wake when supported and otherwise a notice and handoff, not an in-session wait.
findings.fix: Make sections 6–8 of ai-kit-cross-ai the sole retry procedure. For a user-requested hard-tier stop, follow its confirmed one-shot or handoff branch; for a GSD-owned dispatch, report the evidence and leave the retry decision to the caller.

findings.evidence: “pi sets PI_PROVIDER and PI_MODEL only for commands the pi agent runs through its own bash tool” is version-sensitive and has no dated source or live check in the instructions.
findings.fix: Cite the matching pi release's Bash tool source and the date checked for the Bash, bang and RPC distinction, or instruct the agent to check only whether the variables are set in its own Bash tool and avoid generalizing beyond that installation.

findings.evidence: “by default the project dir plus /tmp and $TMPDIR” has no dated vendor citation, and “.git writability unverified” omits that Codex documents .git as read-only in the default workspace-write policy.
findings.fix: Link the dated Codex Agent Approvals and Security documentation at https://developers.openai.com/codex/agent-approvals-security and distinguish the documented defaults from the user's effective writable roots. Retain the instruction to verify the effective boundary before promising it.

findings.evidence: “accepted by opencode v2.0.31” is a dated-by-version observation without a check date or source URL; the installed CLI may differ.
findings.fix: Keep the historical observation labeled as such and cite the official CLI guide at https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/ with the check date, or tell agents to read the installed OpenCode help before making claims about standalone behavior.

findings.evidence: “--mcp-config <file> --strict-mcp-config for claude” states a vendor-specific flag form without pointing to the runner's source label or live help.
findings.fix: Tell the agent to inspect the active template's --describe entry for the Claude MCP form and confirm it against the installed Claude CLI help before promising strict MCP loading.

findings.evidence: “--additional-mcp-config @<file> for copilot” states a separate vendor-specific flag form without a dated source or live check.
findings.fix: Tell the agent to inspect the active template's --describe entry for the Copilot MCP form and check the installed Copilot CLI help before relying on file syntax or describing whether user MCP servers still load.

findings.evidence: “run confirm-skill-role --name <n> --role <r>” leaves the target implicit. The sibling implementation defaults to the shell's current directory, which need not be the project selected by --project-dir; it can write the role into the wrong .aikit/config.toml.
findings.fix: Show both classify-skills and confirm-skill-role with --cwd set to the selected project. Name the project-local .aikit/config.toml write before asking for approval, and use the global layer only when the owner explicitly requests it.
